title: Region traffic redistribution and customer escalation playbook for cross-region model degradations
creator: Anya Patel
description: Purpose: Define an operator-friendly runbook and customer escalation template for situations where one or more regions show sustained model degradation or routing anomalies. Scope covers Hosted API and Dedicated capacity; notes for Private/VPC customers include an assisted-playbook section. This ticket captures playbook steps, communication templates, automated routing knobs, and the short-term fixes (hotpatch candidates) that can be applied during incidents.
steps: Detect: Monitor region-level SLO delta (p50/p95 latency, 5m error rate) and model token drop-off. Trigger threshold: p95 latency > 2x baseline OR error rate increase > 1.5% sustained for 3 minutes.
Triage: On alert, open incident channel (#inc-rr-<region>) and notify oncall. Attach tenant impact query and top 10 tenants by traffic in last 10 minutes.
Scope determination: Run tenant-influence query to determine if degradation is tenant-localized or region-wide. Label incident as 'tenant-local' or 'region-broad'.

Immediate mitigations (low-risk): enable per-tenant soft-throttle for noisy tenants; switch affected tenants to a warm model variant (lower memory/throughput footprint) if they accept degraded latency/quality.

Traffic redistribution: If region-wide and Dedicated pools are impacted, progressively shift traffic in 5% increments using 'soft-shift' route policy to neighboring healthy region with compatible model family. Validate KV cache hit-rate after each step and monitor tail latency.
KV cache resync: If KV cache desync suspected, trigger targeted cache flush for impacted replicas only and allow rebuild from prefix caching. Avoid global cache flush except as last resort.

Circuit controls: Toggle tenant circuit breaker thresholds to drain background batches and prevent head-of-queue stalls. For Dedicated, temporarily reduce max-concurrent-requests per GPU to protect latency SLOs.
Fallbacks: If shifting fails due to model compatibility, fallback to cross-graded quantized variant (documented in model catalog) and notify PM/ML for quality acceptance.
Customer communications: Use the escalation template to notify affected customers within 30 minutes (see attachments). Provide ETA windows for mitigation, and a post-incident summary timeframe.

Hotfix rollout: If a service-level configuration change is validated in staging, prepare a canary in the least critical region and observe for 15 minutes before global rollout. Link PR and release notes in incident channel.

Post-incident: Run automated validation (synthetic prompts and customer prompt-samples if available) against recovered region and mark incident stable only after 2 hours of sustained SLOs. Start postmortem within 72 hours.

Private/VPC customers: For on-prem or VPC customers, coordinate with customer SRE and provide the 'assisted-playbook' checklist; offer remote debugging session and a signed temporary support access token if authorized.
rollback_steps: If traffic shift creates regressions: revert routing policy in reverse increments (5% back every 2 minutes) and restore original region weighting.
If cache flush increased errors: rehydrate from persisted snapshots and roll back to pre-flush KV snapshot. If unavailable, open an engineer-owned ticket to rebuild and notify customers.
If a hotfix causes regressions in canary: abort rollout, revert to previous binary, and create a rollback PR with root-cause notes.
checklist: Create incident channel and pin runbook
List top affected tenants and notify account managers
Apply soft-throttle to noisy tenants as needed
Execute progressive soft-shift with monitoring gates
Validate KV cache and model compatibility at each step
Prepare customer update and postmortem docket
notes: Avoid global model swaps unless all routing fallbacks are exhausted; model compatibility mismatches are a common cause of shifted-traffic failures.
Prefer soft-throttle over immediate tenant eviction to preserve request ordering for conversational workloads.
When shifting traffic across regions, prioritize regions with identical quantization/kernel profiles to minimize cold-start degradation.
Dedicated customers with reserved pools may require contract-aware communication; consult Customer Success before automatic reroutes if SLA forbids cross-region serving.
